query: What review signals predict negative IMDb audience satisfaction?

per_column.name: DirectCondemnation
per_column.rationale: Harsh judgment vs neutral/absent is a linguistic signal extractable from review_text that lies outside the label and plausibly correlates with negative satisfaction without being a restatement of it.

per_column.name: EmotionalDistressSignal
per_column.rationale: Presence of distress language is an observable textual feature distinct from the sentiment label; it carries predictive signal about negativity and is not a deterministic function of label_pos.

per_column.name: WasteRegretLanguage
per_column.rationale: Expressions of wasted time/regret are a concrete lexical pattern in the text, external to the label, plausibly predictive of dissatisfaction.

per_column.name: CriticalTargetBreadth
per_column.rationale: Whether criticism is broad/systematic vs narrow is a text-derived attribute that adds nuance beyond mere polarity and can predict severity of dissatisfaction; not a restatement of the label.

per_column.name: SystemicFailureAttribution
per_column.rationale: Framing of failure as fundamental vs isolated is an extractable rhetorical feature outside the focus variable and plausibly predictive of negative satisfaction.

per_column.name: direct_condemnation_signal
per_column.rationale: This is a near-duplicate of DirectCondemnation (same harsh_judgment vs neutral_or_absent categories); it adds no independent signal beyond the first column.

judge.rationale: Five of the six columns are legitimate, non-leaking textual features that each capture a distinct facet of negativity (condemnation, distress, waste/regret, breadth of criticism, failure attribution) and plausibly predict label_pos. None restates the label deterministically or introduces post-outcome leakage. However, the features are correlated with one another (all proxies for negativity), and the sixth column is a redundant duplicate of the first, so the marginal predictive leverage of the set is moderate rather than high.
